body:
Today's scan turned up zero arbitrage opportunities across the 72 live gold contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket — a quiet day by the tracker's usual standard. That's not surprising once you look at how the books are laid out: nearly every Kalshi strike ladder here (the Gold price on August 31, 2026 and at year end series) is a settle-style market, paying out based on where spot XAU lands at a single future timestamp, while Polymarket's contracts are largely touch markets, paying out if price merely brushes a level at any point during a week or month-long window. Those are different bets on different clocks, so even when a Kalshi settle strike and a Polymarket touch strike sit near the same dollar level, comparing their prices directly is comparing apples to a very similar-looking orange — no free money, just different resolution rules.

Price structure across the ladders looks internally consistent: Kalshi's Aug-31-2026 above strikes decay smoothly from 0.97 bid at $3,931.99 down to a penny at $4,931.99, and the year-end ladder implies a higher expected level than the August one (for example, the $4,300-and-above year-end contract bids 0.65 versus the August $4,291.99 contract at 0.72), which is the normal shape you'd expect if the market thinks gold drifts higher over the back half of 2026 rather than something breaking.

The one thing worth flagging for anyone eyeing a specific line item: several contracts show zero 24-hour volume (many of the far out-of-the-money August strikes, for instance), meaning any bid/ask shown there is a stale or thin quote rather than a tradable market. Total volume is concentrated in a handful of contracts — the Polymarket $3,400 August touch-low (about 2,650 in 24h volume) and the Up or Down on August 17 market (about 1,951) — so that's where the order books are actually deep enough to matter.
headline: No arbitrage found across 72 gold contracts as Kalshi and Polymarket structures diverge
